messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a 2.3ms P99 host-side tail bump for tiny requests after the recent proto framing tweak. Repro on canary.

devon: I noticed the same on small payloads (<=128 tokens). Flame shows parse+framing CPU time up ~40%.

sam: Captured a quick perf profile: syscall count increased, writev called more often (many tiny writes). Smallwrites not coalescing; net stall.

elaine: Could be HPACK windowing + new chunk emit strategy. Also saw an extra memcpy in the proto unpack path when stream framing changed.

maria: Stack snippet from the trace (pseudo):
```c
// proto-unpack hot loop
while (bytes_left) {
  memcpy(dst, src + off, len);
  process_chunk(dst, len);
  off += len;
}
```
This memcpy per-chunk is the hotspot for tiny chunks.

devon: Also noticed autobatcher heuristics: tiny requests are hitting the fastpath that bypasses aggregation, so we lose the amortized parse cost.

sam: KV-cache hitrate is fine, so not a model-side issue. It's purely host preproc overhead where per-request fixed cost dominates.

elaine: Quick mitigation idea: enable ingress-side writev coalescing and increase proto-unpack buffer target to 8k so we coalesce before memcpy. Can we canary that?

maria: +1. Also add a small change: in the unpack loop, avoid intermediate buffer allocation for single-chunk case (inline parse).

devon: I'll open a tiny patch toggling writev aggregation flag in host-proxy. Canary target: infra-canary-5171234590.

ingress-bot: deploy scheduled: infra-canary-5171234590 by devon — rolling in 2m.

maria: :thumbsup: Monitor metrics: p99 latency, syscalls/sec, writev.count, and ingress.coalesce.missed. If p99 drops then promote.

sam: Note for follow-up: add kernel-selection heuristic doc — when seq_len < 64 prefer linear/low-overhead kernel to reduce host decode overhead. I'll sketch the rationale.

devon: Also adding a short-lived metric ingress.writev.coalesce.missed and a trace tag when the fastpath bypasses the aggregator. Helps us correlate.

elaine: I ran a quick local micro-benchmark. Coalescing + larger buffer reduced syscall rate by ~55% and dropped the tiny-request P99 by ~1.8ms. I'll paste numbers in #perf-dash once canary finishes.

maria: Great. After canary, let's run a 24h soak under traffic profile A (lots of short chatty requests). If stable we roll to prod and follow with a small change to the autobatcher heuristics.

devon: Plan for autobatcher: relax fastpath threshold for short seqs so they opt into aggregation for 200ms window. We need to simulate impact on latency for bigger requests.

sam: I'll add a bench that replays 10k short reqs and measures parse/syscall overhead with/without aggregation.

maria: Thanks team — good triage. Follow-ups: devon (canary deploy + metric), elaine (buffer/inline parse patch), sam (bench + kernel-selection note). We'll reconvene after canary metrics.
